questions.question: True or false: In the tradition of the Sages, Miriam is counted among the seven prophetesses.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Miriam, daughter of Amram and Jochebed and the elder sister of Aaron and Moses, was active from the days of the bondage until the journey in the wilderness.

questions.question: According to "Seder Olam," after what was Miriam named?
options: From the word for bitterness (merur): that was when the Egyptians began to embitter the lives of Israel
From "mar-yam" (bitter sea), after the waters of the sea
After her grandmother
From the word for vision (mar'eh), for her prophecy
questions.explanation: In scholarship it is conjectured that the name originates in the Egyptian word mry, "beloved"; other homilies connect it with "meri" (rebellion) and "haramah" (elevation).

questions.question: What did Miriam argue against her father Amram, who had divorced his wife?
options: That he should flee with his family from Egypt
That his decree was harsher than Pharaoh's: Pharaoh decreed against the males, and he also against the females
That he should oppose Pharaoh by force
That he should send Moses to Pharaoh's house
questions.explanation: Amram retracted and took Jochebed back, and all Israel after him. Thus Moses was born.

questions.question: True or false: Miriam supported her father's decision to divorce his wife.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: She stood against him: a stance of faith that rejects despair, even in the face of the leader of the generation.

questions.question: With which of the midwives does the tradition identify Miriam?
options: Shiphrah
Bithiah
Puah
Zipporah
questions.explanation: Puah, who was "po'ah" and soothed the newborn, and also "po'ah" by the Holy Spirit: she prophesies that her mother would bear the savior of Israel.

questions.question: What did Amram do, according to the Midrash, when Moses was placed in the Nile?
options: He ordered her to take him out of the water
He sent her to Pharaoh's daughter
He forbade her to approach the Nile
He slapped Miriam on the head and asked: Where is your prophecy?
questions.explanation: In response, Miriam stood at a distance "to know what would be done to him": an active prophetic stance, not passive waiting.

questions.question: Which gift was given to Israel in the wilderness in Miriam's merit?
options: The well
The manna
The Clouds of Glory
The quail
questions.explanation: Three leaders: the manna in the merit of Moses, the Clouds of Glory in the merit of Aaron, and the well in the merit of Miriam.

questions.question: What happened upon Miriam's death?
options: The Clouds of Glory vanished
The well was withdrawn and the Children of Israel were left without water
The manna ceased to fall
The Ark was captured
questions.explanation: Hence the crisis at the Waters of Meribah, at the end of which Moses struck the rock.

questions.question: True or false: Miriam died in Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: According to "Seder Olam," she died on the 10th of Nisan in the fortieth year after the Exodus from Egypt, by a "death by a kiss."

questions.question: According to the Jerusalem Talmud and the Midrash, where was Miriam's well hidden?
options: In the Dead Sea
In the Jordan
In the Sea of Galilee (Kinneret)
In the Pool of Siloam
questions.explanation: According to the Babylonian Talmud, it is located in the Mediterranean Sea, opposite Mount Carmel.

questions.question: True or false: According to Rashi, the women took timbrels with them already from Egypt.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: They were certain that the Lord would perform miracles for them, and therefore they prepared the timbrels in advance.

questions.question: Why did Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses?
options: Because they envied his leadership
Because they wished to appoint Aaron in his place
Because Moses did not heed their voice in Egypt
Miriam had compassion on Zipporah, who was wronged by Moses' abstinence
questions.explanation: Her mistake was that she did not understand the level of Moses' prophecy, "mouth to mouth," which requires constant abstinence.

questions.question: True or false: Miriam spoke against Moses in public and in his presence.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: She spoke discreetly, between herself and Aaron, and not in his presence so as not to embarrass him, and she was punished nonetheless.

questions.question: What measure-for-measure recompense do the Sages explain in the fact that the people did not journey until Miriam was brought in?
options: She waited an hour by the Nile for Moses, and the people waited for her seven days
She sang to the people at the sea, and the people sang to her
She gave the people water, and the people gave her manna
She raised Moses, and Moses prayed for her
questions.explanation: The entire camp, six hundred thousand men, halted in the wilderness and waited for her purification.

questions.question: True or false: The Rambam counted the remembrance of the incident of Miriam as a separate positive commandment.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The Rambam saw it as part of the prohibition of gossip. It was the Ramban who counted "Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam" as a positive commandment.

questions.question: In which blessing, according to the Ari, should one have in mind the remembrance of the incident of Miriam?
options: "Sim Shalom"
"Ahavah Rabbah," at the words "to thank You"
"Baruch She'amar"
"Aleinu"
questions.explanation: To recall that the mouth was created to give thanks and to unify the Name, and not to speak evil speech with it.

questions.question: According to the "Sefat Emet," how did the women's song differ from the men's song?
options: The women sang in the Egyptian language
The men sang with timbrels and the women with the mouth
The women prepared vessels already during the bondage out of faith, and the men sang in response to the miracle
The women sang only after Miriam's death
questions.explanation: This is faith that sees the future salvation as present in the present, and prepares vessels for it in advance.

questions.question: What does the timbrel symbolize in Kabbalah, and what did Miriam do with it?
options: Joy, which she constricted
Valor, with which she fought Egypt
Prophecy, with which she announced the miracle
The power of constriction and judgment, which she turned into mercy
questions.explanation: With playing and dancing she raised the light from below to above: "returning light" and "itaruta de-letata" (arousal from below).

questions.question: According to "Shemirat HaLashon," what does the word "on the way" teach in the remembrance of the incident of Miriam?
options: That the punishment was not delayed until a place of encampment, but came immediately
That Miriam spoke on the way and not in the tent
That it is permitted to speak while walking
That the people continued on its way without her
questions.explanation: This is one of four components: what He did, to whom He did it, in what place, and at what time. From here follows an a fortiori inference for one who speaks ill of his fellow in public.

questions.question: Why, according to the Magen Avraham, did they not institute a special public reading for the remembrance of the incident of Miriam?
options: Because it is not a commandment at all
Out of respect for the honor of Miriam the righteous
Because remembrance in the heart suffices
Because it is read on Purim
questions.explanation: One fulfills the obligation through the annual reading of the portions Beha'alotekha and Ki Teitzei, and in the prayer books it is among the "six remembrances."
